title: Phase transitions of the antiferromagnetic $J_1$-$J_2$-$J_3$ Ising model on the cubic lattice
authors: Kai-Wei Huang, Chien-Ting Chen, Shang-Wei Li, Fu-Jiun Jiang
abstract: Motivated by the conflicting findings in prior studies regarding the nature of the phase transition for the three-dimensional antiferromagnetic $J_1$-$J_2$-$J_3$ Ising model on the cubic lattice with $J_1 = J_2 = J_3 = 1.0$, in this study we conduct a detailed investigation of this model using both Monte Carlo simulations and neural networks (NN). Here $J_1$ and $J_2$ are the intralayer nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor couplings, respectively, and $J_3$ is the nearest-neighbor interlayer interaction. By investigating the data obtained from much larger lattices than those used in previous studies, we find that the phase transition for $J_1 = J_2 = J_3 = 1.0$ is second order without any ambiguity. Hence we bring a resolution to this debate. Apart from $J_1 = J_2 = J_3 = 1.0$, we study the critical phenomenon associated with $J_2/J_1 = 4/7$ and $J_3 = J_1 = 1.0$ as well. In addition, by employing a dedicated training and testing strategy, our NN computation not only is much more efficient than those utilizing the standard procedures commonly used in the literature, but also requires only a per-mille fraction of the storage capacity needed by a conventional NN calculation when a large linear system size $L$ is considered. The method employed here provides an extremely resource-efficient route for applying NN techniques to study the critical behaviors of higher-dimensional systems.
summary: This work resolves a long-standing debate on the phase transition order of the 3D $J_1$-$J_2$-$J_3$ Ising model by combining Monte Carlo simulations and efficient Neural Network calculations. The study confirms the transition is second order for the isotropic case ($J_1=J_2=J_3=1.0$) and first order for $J_2=4/7$. The NN method is highlighted as a powerful, resource-saving tool for studying critical behavior in high-dimensional systems.
main_problem: The study aims to resolve conflicting historical findings regarding the order of the phase transition in the three-dimensional antiferromagnetic $J_1$-$J_2$-$J_3$ Ising model on the cubic lattice.
main_result: The authors conclude that for the isotropic case ($J_1 = J_2 = J_3 = 1.0$), the phase transition is second order, while for $J_2 = 4/7$, it is first order.
method: The research employs a combination of extensive Monte Carlo simulations and a novel, resource-efficient Neural Network (NN) technique to analyze critical behavior.
model_or_system: The system is the 3D antiferromagnetic $J_1$-$J_2$-$J_3$ Ising model on the cubic lattice, described by a Hamiltonian involving nearest-neighbor ($J_1, J_3$) and next-nearest-neighbor ($J_2$) couplings.
key_observables: Energy density histograms, specific heat ($C_v$) scaling, and a diagnostic observable $R$ derived from NN calculations.
important_parameters: The couplings $J_1, J_2, J_3$, particularly the isotropic case ($J_1 = J_2 = J_3 = 1.0$) and the specific ratio $J_2/J_1 = 4/7$.
main_assumptions: The NN method is shown to be highly efficient, requiring minimal storage capacity compared to standard procedures for large lattices.
figures_summary: Figures show energy histograms diagnosing first-order transitions (two-peak structure) for $J_2=4/7$, and continuous evolution of the observable $R$ across $T_c$ for $J_2=1.0$, supporting a second-order transition.
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates the phase transition order using both MC and NN methods, first resolving the $J_1=J_2=J_3=1.0$ case, then analyzing the $J_2=4/7$ case, and finally confirming the second-order nature for $J_2=1.0$ using large-scale testing sets.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of advanced numerical techniques like Neural Networks to resolve long-standing debates in classical statistical mechanics models is valuable for understanding critical phenomena in complex lattice systems.
